action: Tested a two-ref non-force fast-forward protocol against one compliant concurrency/stale-writer model and one force-capable rewrite model using only own CLEAN state and public GitHub reference API documentation.
result: Conditional protocol safety only: stale divergent writers are rejected by non-fast-forward protection; a surviving second cross-linked ref can detect one-ref rewrite; shared serialization remains, separate REST updates have a torn-update window, and coherent force rewind of both refs defeats exact rollback detection.
tested_scope: Two refs, two protocol-compliant concurrent writers from common heads, one stale divergent writer, one separate-REST partial transition, and one actor able to force-move either/both refs; no live ref mutation or protected/admin authority.
conflict_check: Own role-local checkpoint and immutable own receipt only; no O/downstream/other-worker semantics and no scheduler/protected authority mutation.
continuation: Fresh-bootstrap and test GitHub GraphQL updateRefs as atomic two-ref beforeOid CAS with force=false for protocol participants, then retain the force-capable dual-rewrite impossibility boundary and separately fail-closed on scheduled-Chat callability if the mutation surface is not exposed.
